title: A finite type domain over a field has the dimension of each of its local rings at maximal ideals
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] which is an integral domain. Then for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset S$ the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] of the localization $S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] equals the Krull dimension of $S$: $\dim(S_{\mathfrak m})=\dim(S)$, and this is a non-negative integer. Equivalently, every maximal chain of prime ideals of $S$ (a chain $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_t$ of prime ideals that cannot be lengthened by inserting a prime ideal before $\mathfrak q_0$, between two consecutive members, or after $\mathfrak q_t$) has length $t=\dim(S)$.

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks Algebra 00OS (algebra.tex line 27763), tags 00OS/00OQ/00OR/00OP verified in tags/tags. Mathlib has no statement that every maximal ideal of a finite type domain over a field has height dim S (only Ideal.exists_isMaximal_height: some maximal ideal), nor catenarity; the source repository has none either. Proof: S = k[x_1..x_n]/p (step 1, correspondence of primes); chains of P have length <= n via dim P_M = n (00OP/00OQ, existing node) (step 2); ht(M) = n (step 3); a longest chain below m is saturated from (0) to m, its preimage a maximal chain from p to M, so dim S_m = n - ht(p) by 00OR (new unsplit node) (step 4); dim S = n - ht(p) (step 5); the maximal-chain formulation (step 6). New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-chain-height-difference (00OR, unsplit) and lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal (00E0, Mathlib leaf Ideal.exists_le_maximal). Statement unchanged in substance; clarified 'maximal chain' and that the dimension is a non-negative integer.

reviewed: pass (L, 2026-10-10): 6 steps follow 00OS: chains in P = k[x] have length <= n (00OP/00OQ localization dimension, new leaf for maximal ideals), ht(M) = n, every maximal chain from p to M has length n - ht(p) (00OR, new unsplit node), so dim S_m = n - ht(p) = dim S. Statement wording clarified only.
